131.plain: A pretrained 3D generative model encodes an object and predicts colored labels on its reconstructed surface; these colors act as part indicators. The system learns part segmentation by repurposing the model's internal structure knowledge without annotated training data for the segmentation task itself.

132.plain: Light bouncing many times through dense hair is expensive to track; instead, treat the hair as a participating medium that scatters light, and stochastically sample one scattering event to approximate higher-order bounces while using explicit fiber geometry for direct lighting detail.

133.plain: Users sketch how articulated parts should move (arrows, strokes), and the system infers movable parts and their motion parameters by learning to map 2D sketch intention to 3D part discovery and motion constraints, without needing object category labels.

134.plain: Recovering material and lighting from images is a high-variance, brittle optimization problem; a spatial blending field interpolates locally between cached radiance estimates and standard unbiased samplers, reducing variance while keeping slope well-behaved for reliable parameter recovery.

135.plain: Neutron transport is computed by summing light arriving from all possible paths through matter; the paper uses random sampling to estimate how each path changes with respect to design choices, then follows the slope downhill to optimize shielding and material layouts.

136.plain: Finding nearest neighbors in point clouds is sped up by building a recursive network of neighborhoods, where each point remembers which others it's close to; the method exploits this structure to skip far-away points without checking them.

137.plain: Shape deformation is expressed as a smooth flow (like water moving through space) using an invertible a system that learns from examples that learns how every point transforms continuously over time without tangling or tearing.

138.plain: Finding where two complex surfaces intersect and controlling precision means bounding how far the true curve strays from our approximation using curvature measures and geometric hulls that must all satisfy distance limits at once.

139.plain: Fluid motion is optimized by following the slope that lowers error, but the paper shortcuts the backward pass by noticing that the flow map's cross-step connections carry slope information far more efficiently than computing every intermediate step's contribution.

140.plain: Hologram patterns are designed by solving one enormous system balancing wave physics (how light bends through space) and chemistry (how material hardens or dissolves) at once, optimizing the phase pattern to pre-correct for blurring.

141.plain: Human image generation learns a smooth path from noise to images while obeying topological constraints that enforce anatomically plausible bone ratios and joint angles, so the body always stays structurally valid.

142.plain: Finding a shape's natural vibration modes—the ways it likes to wiggle—requires solving enormous natural-mode equations; the paper accelerates this by borrowing multigrid methods that solve problems at coarse and fine scales together.

143.plain: Cloth geometry is reconstructed by deforming a template 3D model into the shape where elastic strain plus contact constraints are minimized, solved by balancing forces at every point simultaneously.

144.plain: Meshing a smooth surface on a fixed grid captures thin features by encoding surface connectivity via integer intersection counts on edges—a topological trick that bypasses the usual frequency limits of grids.

145.plain: Signed distance to point clouds is computed by fitting each point with a torus (which has a closed-form distance formula), using a a system that learns from examples to predict local curvature, enabling fast queries without global optimization.

146.plain: Video generation learns to conditionally denoise many modalities at once by randomly masking some as clean guidance and others as targets during training, so the model learns bidirectional mappings between any modalities.

147.plain: Offset surfaces that preserve sharp features are computed by generating offset vertices and triangles via energy minimization that balances distance accuracy with sharp corner preservation, supporting variable offset distances.

148.plain: Constant mean curvature surfaces (elegant shapes with balanced bending) are built by discretizing the classical fact that their normal maps are harmonic—i.e., as smooth as possible—solved via energy minimization and Poisson equations.

149.plain: Motion style transfer decomposes pose changes into static posture and frame-by-frame temporal dynamics, learning each component from seconds of paired data via a system that learns from examples that generalize to new motions under style control.

150.plain: The system learns to predict hand pose and motion by identifying patterns in image data, using relationships between the two hands to reason about their interaction. It builds these relationships through attention—finding which hand parts matter most for predicting each other's position.

151.plain: The method evolves an image step-by-step from noise toward a realistic material by learning patterns from training examples. It uses depth and lighting information as constraints that guide the transformation, ensuring the output matches the target material's appearance under different conditions.

152.plain: The method discovers how a deformable object naturally evolves over time by finding its fundamental vibration patterns, then uses those patterns to skip ahead through time instead of solving step-by-step equations. This trades slow sequential solving for fast repeated multiplications.
